title: A business owned by First Nations Australians

draft.title: First Nations Australians in business
card: Many First Nations Australians run businesses. They work in areas such as tourism, art, food and construction.
A tourism business may guide visitors on Country and share stories and knowledge. An art business may sell paintings or crafts.
Many of these businesses aim to create jobs, often for people in their communities.
They may also support their communities in other ways, such as passing on culture.
draft.remember: Many First Nations businesses create jobs and support their communities.

a.q: A First Nations family runs a tour business, and hires young people from their town as guides. What is one reason for this business?
opts: To create jobs for their community
To avoid selling anything to visitors
To make only goods and no services
To keep all work within one family
a.why: Hiring local young people creates jobs in the community, which many First Nations businesses aim to do. Guiding visitors is a service that is sold, so the other options are wrong.

b.q: Which of these is an area where many First Nations Australians run businesses?
opts: Art
Only farming
Only mining
Only banking
b.why: Art is one area named on the card, along with tourism, food and construction. The other options use only, which wrongly limits the areas, and the card does not name them.
b.clue: Look at the list of areas on the card.

a.best: To create jobs for their community

problems.detail: Every wrong option begins with 'Only' and 'Art' is the only one without it. A student can pick the answer from that pattern alone, without knowing the idea. The absolute word 'only' also contrasts with the card's 'such as' list.

The distractors are implausible for a tour business ('avoid selling anything to visitors', 'make only goods and no services'), so the right answer is obvious without understanding the card. 'Only' in a distractor also adds absolute wording.

The why says 'Guiding visitors is a service that is sold, so the other options are wrong'. That does not explain why 'To keep all work within one family' is wrong (it is wrong because they hire young people from the town). It also leans on the goods/services idea from point 2.

check.summary: The card and answers are accurate. In question b, only the right option lacks 'Only', which gives it away, and question a's distractors are too implausible. The why for (a) does not explain why the 'one family' option is wrong.

proposal.title: First Nations Australians in business
card: Many First Nations Australians run businesses. They work in areas such as tourism, art, food and construction.
A tourism business may guide visitors on Country, meaning traditional lands and waters. A construction business may build homes or roads.
Many of these businesses aim to create jobs, often for people in their own communities.
They may also support their communities in other ways, such as passing on culture.
proposal.remember: Many First Nations businesses create jobs and support their communities.

a.q: A First Nations family runs a tour business. They hire young people from their town as guides. Which aim does this hiring show?
opts: Creating jobs for people in their community
Keeping all of the work inside one family
Bringing in workers from other places
Cutting the number of people they employ
a.why: The family gives guide jobs to young people from their own town, which creates jobs in the community. It is not keeping work in one family, because the guides come from outside the family.
a.clue: Where do the new guides come from?

b.q: Dan, a First Nations man in Alice Springs, owns a building company. He trains young local workers. What area is his business, and what aim does it show?
opts: Construction, and creating local jobs
Tourism, and creating local jobs
Construction, and keeping work in one family
Food, and bringing in outside workers
b.why: Building things is construction, and training young local workers creates jobs in his community. Tourism is tempting because the business is in a well known town, but Dan builds things rather than guiding visitors.
b.clue: What does Dan's company actually do each day?
